author: David Bombal
description:
This looks like a normal USB-C Ethernet adapter and hub, but inside is a Linux computer built for penetration testing.

@DarrenKitchen from @hak5 shows me the new LAN Turtle Hub, which can provide remote access, sniff network traffic, intercept USB devices and even exfiltrate files, all while continuing to work like a normal Ethernet adapter.

The scary part? The user may have no idea anything is happening.

Use tools like this only on systems you own or have explicit permission to test.

#Cybersecurity #Hacking #Hak5
title: This USB Adapter Can Hack Your Network

Marcus Hutchins is back, and this time we talk about AI, hacking, VPNs, ransomware, EDR killers, public Wi-Fi security, juice jacking, AI slop, and where cybersecurity is heading.

Marcus explains how a North Korean hacking group was able to use AI for malware-related tasks while the same AI refused to help him analyze that malware. He also explains why he believes many VPN security claims are misleading, why public Wi-Fi is not as dangerous as many people think, and why some captive portal attacks cannot be stopped by a VPN.
